title: Minimal fallback surface and telemetry PRD brainstorm
content:
Overview

This is a focused brainstorming PRD for a minimal, developer-friendly fallback surface for the Hosted API streaming call path, paired with a compact telemetry contract that makes diagnosis of partial streams and tool-call fallbacks practical. The idea is to ship a small, opinionated API that lets client SDKs and apps gracefully recover from degraded model/region/tool availability while keeping structured output semantics intact.

Why this matters
- Customers build interactive, tool-driven features that cannot tolerate silent truncation or inconsistent tool-call results.
- Many failure modes are operational (region capacity, model OOM, tool timeout) and need standard, debuggable handoffs.
- Existing designs either force heavy client logic or leak server-side complexity into SDKs. We want a thin, deterministic surface that SDKs can implement once and rely on.

Goals
- Define a minimal wire contract for partial/failed streaming responses and deterministic fallback markers.
- Provide clear SDK ergonomics for Python and JS that minimize client code while exposing enough metadata for retries and observability.
- Specify telemetry fields that tie a user interaction to model variant, region, tool invocation id, and fallback reason.
- Preserve structured-output envelopes so downstream parsers have reliable markers for partial vs final payloads.

Non-goals
- This is not a full rewrite of streaming framing or session handoff; keep changes additive and backward compatible.
- Not attempting to invent new tool orchestration DSLs. We only standardize existing best-effort handoffs.

User stories
- As a product engineer, I want the SDK to raise a typed error when a tool call times out mid-stream, including the partial JSON that was emitted so I can surface it to users.
- As an ops engineer, I want telemetry that shows which model variant and region served a request and whether a fallback model was used, so I can correlate increased fallbacks with capacity events.
- As a third-party integrator, I want a compact, language-agnostic marker that indicates a server-side fallback so my client can either retry or show an explanatory UI.

High level design
- Streaming envelope: every streaming frame is either DATA, CHECKPOINT, or SIGNAL.
  - DATA: application payload fragment (may be text, delta JSON, binary chunk).
  - CHECKPOINT: lightweight snapshot of parsed structured output so clients can update UI mid-stream. CHECKPOINTs are optional and limited to small JSON deltas.
  - SIGNAL: meta-events such as TOOL_START, TOOL_RESULT, FALLBACK_ENTER, FALLBACK_EXIT, STREAM_TERMINATED. SIGNAL frames carry a small key-value map with predefined keys.

- Fallback marker: SIGNAL: FALLBACK_ENTER with fields: reason, from_variant, to_variant, truncated: boolean, partial_checksum. Clients must treat this as authoritative: subsequent DATA frames may come from the fallback variant.

- Partial output preservation: if a tool call fails mid-stream, server emits SIGNAL: TOOL_ABORT with tool_id, tool_call_id, reason, and includes the last CHECKPOINT. Client SDK surfaces this as a resumable record; product teams can decide whether to reattempt tool execution or show the partial result to users.

API surface (proposal)
- POST /v1/responses (existing): keep same, but stream frames as newline-prefixed objects with type field. Backcompat: if client passes header Accept: application/x-redwood-stream-v2, server will emit SIGNAL/CHECKPOINT frames.

- New query parameters / headers
  - x-rw-stream-version: 2 (negotiates frame semantics)
  - x-rw-session-tags: comma-separated list (client provided tags to be echoed in telemetry)

SDK ergonomics (opinionated minimal API)
- Python (sync streaming helper):
  - with client.stream_response(...) as stream:
      for frame in stream.frames():
          if frame.type == "DATA": yield frame.payload
          if frame.type == "SIGNAL" and frame.signal == "FALLBACK_ENTER":
              # callback or error object with reason and partial state
              stream.on_fallback(frame.meta)
- JS (async iterator):
  - const stream = client.streamResponse(opts)
    for await (const frame of stream) {
      if (frame.type === 'DATA') render(frame.payload)
      if (frame.type === 'SIGNAL' && frame.signal === 'TOOL_ABORT') {
        showPartial(frame.meta.checkpoint)
      }
    }
- SDKs should provide a single high-level convenience mode: "resumable-tool-calls: auto" which attempts transparent server-side resume when supported, falling back to surfacing a TOOL_ABORT with a resume token.

Telemetry contract (compact, high-signal)
- Each request and fallback must emit the following minimal fields (logged and available in Console):
  - request_id (UUID)
  - session_tags (string list)
  - model_variant (string)
  - region (string)
  - fallback_path: enum none | variant_swap | tool_offload | degraded_mode
  - fallback_reason: short code (CAPACITY, TIMEOUT, OOM, TOOL_ERROR, AUTH_FAIL)
  - tool_call_id (if applicable)
  - partial_checksum: short hex (if partial output emitted)
- Sampling strategy: full telemetry for any request that enters a fallback_path; lightweight sampled telemetry (1%) for clean success paths.

Error and fallback semantics matrix
- Model OOM: emit FALLBACK_ENTER to a smaller quantized variant with truncated flag true; include last CHECKPOINT. Telemetry: fallback_path=variant_swap, fallback_reason=OOM.
- Tool timeout: emit TOOL_ABORT with tool_call_id and last CHECKPOINT; fallback_path=tool_offload, fallback_reason=TIMEOUT.
- Region capacity: try sibling region within same tier, emit FALLBACK_ENTER + region meta; fallback_path=variant_swap or degraded_mode depending on config.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics
- SDK surfaces a deterministic fallback marker in 100% of simulated failure tests in CI.
- Console shows per-request fallback rates by model_variant and region within 1 hour of event.
- Customer engineering report: fewer than 5% of interactive sessions produce opaque partials (i.e., partial output without a SIGNAL) within 90 days of rollout.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0: server emits SIGNAL frames behind feature flag; SDKs can opt-in via header. Internal rollout to Redwood product teams for dogfooding.
- Phase 1: enable on 10% of hosted traffic for non-critical tiers; collect telemetry and SDK feedback.
- Phase 2: widen to 50%, add Console visualizations for fallback heatmaps.
- Phase 3: default on for all new stream clients; maintain compatibility mode for legacy clients.

Operational and privacy notes
- Telemetry fields must avoid PII. session_tags are limited to developer-provided alphanumeric tokens only; SDKs should refuse or redact if tags look like emails or long text.
- Partial checkpoints are size-limited (max 2KB) and must not include attachments or binary blobs.

Risks and mitigation
- Signal spam: many small SIGNAL frames could increase client CPU. Mitigation: rate-limit SIGNAL emission server-side and batch meta into periodic CHECKPOINTs.
- Client fragmentation: different SDKs may implement different fallback UIs. Mitigation: ship reference UI components and sample code in the developer playbook.
- Backcompat complexity: some clients will not negotiate v2 stream. Mitigation: maintain v1 behavior and provide a graceful downgrade path.

Open questions
- Do we want server-side automatic retries of tool calls, or leave that decision to the client? Recommendation: allow server-side optional auto-retry under operator-configured policies, but always emit TOOL_ABORT and a resume token if retry was attempted.
- Is the partial_checksum strong enough for client-side dedup and resume logic? Evaluate moving to a short deterministic snapshot id if resume flows require stronger guarantees.

Implementation notes for Eng
- Small change to streaming pipeline: add signal framing layer after tokenizer pipeline but before response mux. Ensure signals flow on the same socket stream and are newline-delimited JSON to preserve simple client parsing.
- Add telemetry hook that tags fallback events with deterministic codes; instrument canary dashboards and alert rules for sudden spikes.

Next steps (short term)
- Align with serving runtime on signal semantics and a compact in-band schema (IETF style keyset) by 2025-03-20.
- Design Python/JS SDK primitives and prototype a reference UI widget by 2025-04-10.
- Create a small test harness that injects failure modes and verifies signals are emitted and surfaced in SDKs.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally lightweight and additive. Feedback requested on SIGNAL key names, sampling thresholds for telemetry, and whether auto-retry should be opt-in or opt-out.

-- end of brainstorm --
